name: Balsamic Roasted Pork with Grapes, Carrot Fritters & Basil Yogurt

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
454 g red grapes
6 medium carrots
1 lemon
1 small pkg fresh basil

instructions.primary_message: Halve grapes and place in a medium bowl.

Pat pork chops dry with paper towels. Large dice and add to the bowl with the grapes along with oil, vinegar, and spices. Stir to combine, transfer to a large baking dish, and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 pork chops, boneless
extra virgin olive oil
4 tsp balsamic vinegar
1 tsp sage, dried
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking dish in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, stirring halfway, until pork is cooked through and grapes are soft, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place eggs, milk, and oil in a clean medium bowl. Whisk to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 eggs
118 ml whole milk
extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Add flour, salt, and baking powder to the bowl with the egg mixture. Whisk once more until the batter is just combined.
Peel, trim, and coarsely grate carrots. Add to the bowl with the batter and gently stir until incorporated.
Preheat a large skillet over medium heat. Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom.

Working in batches, using a ¼-cup measure, drop batter into the skillet, spacing scoops a few inches apart; flatten slightly with the back of a spoon. Cook, flipping once, until fritters are golden brown, 3-5 minutes. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate.
Meanwhile, juice lemon into a small bowl.

Pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the bowl with the lemon juice along with yogurt and spices. Stir to combine the yogurt sauce and set aside. (Reserve remaining basil for serving.)
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup plain Greek yogurt
½ tsp garlic powder
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Divide pork, grapes, and carrot fritters between plates. Sprinkle pork with reserved basil and serve with yogurt sauce on the side. Enjoy!
